description: Large geostationary bus with two solar wings and reflector antennas (e.g. Express-AM, Intelsat). Carries a 490 N apogee engine.
name: Communications satellite

description: Optical imaging spacecraft in a sun-synchronous orbit (e.g. Resurs-P, WorldView).
name: Earth-observation satellite

description: GNSS spacecraft for MEO constellations (e.g. GLONASS-K, GPS III).
name: Navigation satellite

description: Space observatory or research platform (e.g. Spektr-RG, Fermi).
name: Science / astronomy satellite

description: Rideshare dispenser releasing a cluster of small satellites. No propulsion of its own.
name: CubeSat rideshare dispenser

description: Flat-packed stack of broadband satellites; the launcher upper stage performs the orbit raising.
name: Starlink batch (60 × 260 kg)

description: Crew capsule with service module (e.g. Soyuz MS, Crew Dragon). Raises its own orbit to the station with a 3.9 kN engine.
name: Crewed spacecraft

description: The first artificial satellite: a 58 cm polished sphere with four whip antennas and two radio transmitters. No propulsion.
name: Sputnik-1 (PS-1)

description: Gagarin's Vostok: a 2.3 m descent sphere on an instrument module. Its TDU-1 engine only brought it home, so Blok E put it in orbit.
name: Vostok 3KA

description: Apollo 11: command and service module, the lunar module and its adapter, 45.7 t. The S-IVB made the translunar injection; the service engine was kept for the Moon.
name: Apollo CSM + LM
